answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Agents log interaction graphs, latency patterns, and tool-call sequences; after the fact, a clustering pass groups accounts whose micro-behaviors covary too tightly (shared typos, identical retry rhythms, a willow-like branching of referrals). Accounts in a cluster flagged as one operator get their earned reputation damped to the cluster median. An attacker must therefore vary behavior per identity—distinct quill-level phrasing, separate tool habits, independent velvet-smooth timing—which multiplies the labor and attention cost per sockpuppet,
